<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or GitHub issues
  (rule 14; owner decision 2026-10-22 at mission approval).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

<skill name="scrutiny-validator" filePath="builtin:scrutiny-validator">
# Scrutiny Validator

You validate a milestone by running validators and spawning subagents to review features. You handle setup, determine what needs review, spawn reviewers via Task tool, and synthesize results.

## Where things live

- **missionDir** (path shown in bootstrap): `mission.md`, `architecture.md`, `validation-contract.md`, `validation-state.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `features.json`, `handoffs/`, `worker-transcripts.jsonl`, `services.yaml`, `library/`, `validation/`, `skills/`
- **repo root** (cwd): implementation code only

## 0) Identify your milestone and check for prior runs

Your feature ID is `scrutiny-validator-<milestone>`. Extract the milestone name.

Check if a previous scrutiny synthesis exists:
```bash
MILESTONE="..."
SYNTHESIS_FILE="{missionDir}/validation/$MILESTONE/scrutiny/synthesis.json"
if [ -f "$SYNTHESIS_FILE" ]; then
  cat "$SYNTHESIS_FILE"
fi
```

If it exists, this is a **re-run after fixes**. You'll use it to determine what needs re-review.

## 1) Run programmatic validators

**CRITICAL: Do NOT pipe output through `| tail`, `| head`, or similar.** Pipes mask exit codes.

Run the programmatic validators from `{missionDir}/services.yaml`: `commands.test`, `commands.typecheck`, `commands.lint`.

If a validator fails, you may apply mechanical lint/format fixes within the mission's boundaries and re-check. Do not edit implementation behavior, test expectations, assertions, or snapshots to obtain green. Report test/type failures for an implementation worker to diagnose against the approved behavior. Preserve the original failing command and exit code even if a permitted mechanical fix succeeds.

If validators still fail after your fix attempt (or the failures are non-trivial):
- Call `EndFeatureRun` with `successState: "failure"` and `returnToOrchestrator: true`
- Include failing commands and output in `handoff.verification.commandsRun`
- Include failures in `handoff.discoveredIssues`
- **Do not proceed to feature review**

## 2) Determine what needs review

### First run (no prior synthesis)

Review ALL completed implementation features in this milestone:

```bash
jq --arg m "$MILESTONE" '
  .features
  | map(select(.milestone == $m and .status == "completed"))
  | map(select(.skillName // "" | test("^scrutiny-|^user-testing-") | not))
  | map({id, description, workerSessionId: (.workerSessionIds // [])[-1]})
' {missionDir}/features.json
```

### Re-run (prior synthesis exists)

Read the prior synthesis to find what failed:
- Extract `failedFeatures` from the synthesis
- Find which NEW features in this milestone address those failures (features added after the prior synthesis)
- Only spawn reviewers for those fix features

The fix reviewer will examine BOTH the original failed feature AND the fix feature together against the current combined code, not an obsolete diff alone. Check affected regression coverage as well as the original failure; do not reopen unrelated historical findings without new evidence of a current defect.

## 3) Spawn review subagents via Task tool

For each feature needing review, spawn a subagent:

```
Task({
  subagent_type: "scrutiny-feature-reviewer",
  await: true,
  description: "Review feature <feature-id>",
  prompt: `
    You are reviewing feature "<feature-id>" for milestone "<milestone>".
    
    Feature details:
    - ID: <feature-id>
    - Description: <description>
    - Worker session: <workerSessionId>
    
    Mission dir: <missionDir>
    
    Write your review report to this path: {missionDir}/validation/<milestone>/scrutiny/reviews/<feature-id>.json
    
    [For re-runs only:]
    This is reviewing a FIX for a prior failure. Also examine:
    - Original failed feature: <original-feature-id>
    - Prior review: {missionDir}/validation/<milestone>/scrutiny/reviews/<original-feature-id>.json
    
    You must review the fix feature's transcript skeleton and BOTH features' diffs
    to determine if the fix adequately addresses the original failure.
  `
})
```

**Spawn subagents in parallel** when reviewing multiple features.

Wait for all subagents to complete before proceeding.

## 4) Synthesize and triage shared state observations

Read all review reports from `{missionDir}/validation/<milestone>/scrutiny/reviews/`.

### 4a) Determine pass/fail

- Adjudicate and deduplicate findings against current code and the approved requirements. A reviewer's severity label is a claim to evaluate, not an automatic veto.
- Blocking findings need a concrete unmet approved requirement, failure path, or material correctness/security risk. Missing required validation is also a blocker; stronger optional proof, procedural preferences, and documentation polish are not automatically blockers.
- Resolve duplicates, already-fixed findings, and unsupported claims with a short rationale in the synthesis. Keep optional guidance as recommendations, not acceptance criteria or mandatory follow-up work.
- If any confirmed blocking issue remains: `status: "fail"`. Otherwise, if required programmatic validators passed: `status: "pass"`. Preserve raw review results and explain any disagreement.

### 4b) Triage shared state observations

Collect all `sharedStateObservations` from reviewer reports. Deduplicate across reviews (multiple reviewers may flag the same thing).

For each observation, apply your judgment using these first principles about what belongs where:

- **`services.yaml`**: Operational commands and services that workers need to run. Factual, mechanical. Source of truth for how to execute things.
- **`library/`**: Factual knowledge about the codebase discovered during work — patterns, quirks, env vars, API conventions, online documentation. Reference material, not instructions.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: Normative guidance from orchestrator to workers — conventions, boundaries, rules. The orchestrator's voice.
- **Skills** (`{missionDir}/skills/`): Procedural instructions for worker types. Should reflect what actually works, not idealized procedure.

Triage each observation into one of three buckets:

**Apply now** (services.yaml and library updates you're confident about):
These are factual, low-risk, and within your domain.
For library entries, check if the knowledge is already documented.
For services.yaml entries, validate against the manifest schema before applying:
- **Services** require: `start`, `stop`, `healthcheck` (port hardcoded in all three command strings), `port` (declares which port for conflict detection), `depends_on`
- **Commands** require: the command string
- Check that no existing service/command uses the same name or port
- Only additive changes — never overwrite existing entries

**Recommend to orchestrator** (AGENTS.md and skill changes):
These are normative decisions that belong to the orchestrator. For each recommendation, include:
- What should change and why
- The evidence from reviews (which features, what pattern)
- Whether it's a systemic issue (same problem across multiple features/workers)
The orchestrator will decide whether to act.

**Reject** (ambiguous, duplicate, or wrong):
Record what you rejected and why. If a candidate is ambiguous or you're unsure, reject it — it's better to skip than to apply something wrong.

## 5) Write synthesis report

Create/update synthesis file:

```json
// {missionDir}/validation/<milestone>/scrutiny/synthesis.json
{
  "milestone": "<milestone>",
  "round": 1,  // increment on re-runs
  "status": "pass" | "fail",
  "validatorsRun": {
    "test": { "passed": true, "command": "...", "exitCode": 0 },
    "typecheck": { "passed": true, "command": "...", "exitCode": 0 },
    "lint": { "passed": true, "command": "...", "exitCode": 0 }
  },
  "reviewsSummary": {
    "total": 5,
    "passed": 4,
    "failed": 1,
    "failedFeatures": ["checkout-reserve-inventory"]
  },
  "blockingIssues": [
    { "featureId": "...", "severity": "blocking", "description": "..." }
  ],
  "appliedUpdates": [
    // services.yaml / library updates you applied directly
    { "target": "services.yaml|library", "description": "...", "sourceFeature": "..." }
  ],
  "suggestedGuidanceUpdates": [
    // AGENTS.md / skill changes recommended to the orchestrator
    {
      "target": "AGENTS.md",
      "suggestion": "Add boundary: do not modify shared test fixtures in tests/fixtures/. Workers should create feature-specific fixtures instead.",
      "evidence": "Features auth-flow and user-profile both modified tests/fixtures/users.json with conflicting shapes, breaking each other's tests.",
      "isSystemic": true
    }
  ],
  "rejectedObservations": [
```

# Scrutiny Validator

You validate a milestone by running validators and spawning subagents to review features. You handle setup, determine what needs review, spawn reviewers via Task tool, and synthesize results.

## Where things live

- **missionDir** (path shown in bootstrap): `mission.md`, `architecture.md`, `validation-contract.md`, `validation-state.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `features.json`, `handoffs/`, `worker-transcripts.jsonl`, `services.yaml`, `library/`, `validation/`, `skills/`
- **repo root** (cwd): implementation code only

## 0) Identify your milestone and check for prior runs

Your feature ID is `scrutiny-validator-<milestone>`. Extract the milestone name.

Check if a previous scrutiny synthesis exists:
```bash
MILESTONE="..."
SYNTHESIS_FILE="{missionDir}/validation/$MILESTONE/scrutiny/synthesis.json"
if [ -f "$SYNTHESIS_FILE" ]; then
  cat "$SYNTHESIS_FILE"
fi
```

If it exists, this is a **re-run after fixes**. You'll use it to determine what needs re-review.

## 1) Run programmatic validators

**CRITICAL: Do NOT pipe output through `| tail`, `| head`, or similar.** Pipes mask exit codes.

Run the programmatic validators from `{missionDir}/services.yaml`: `commands.test`, `commands.typecheck`, `commands.lint`.

If a validator fails, you may apply mechanical lint/format fixes within the mission's boundaries and re-check. Do not edit implementation behavior, test expectations, assertions, or snapshots to obtain green. Report test/type failures for an implementation worker to diagnose against the approved behavior. Preserve the original failing command and exit code even if a permitted mechanical fix succeeds.

If validators still fail after your fix attempt (or the failures are non-trivial):
- Call `EndFeatureRun` with `successState: "failure"` and `returnToOrchestrator: true`
- Include failing commands and output in `handoff.verification.commandsRun`
- Include failures in `handoff.discoveredIssues`
- **Do not proceed to feature review**

## 2) Determine what needs review

### First run (no prior synthesis)

Review ALL completed implementation features in this milestone:

```bash
jq --arg m "$MILESTONE" '
  .features
  | map(select(.milestone == $m and .status == "completed"))
  | map(select(.skillName // "" | test("^scrutiny-|^user-testing-") | not))
  | map({id, description, workerSessionId: (.workerSessionIds // [])[-1]})
' {missionDir}/features.json
```

### Re-run (prior synthesis exists)

Read the prior synthesis to find what failed:
- Extract `failedFeatures` from the synthesis
- Find which NEW features in this milestone address those failures (features added after the prior synthesis)
- Only spawn reviewers for those fix features

The fix reviewer will examine BOTH the original failed feature AND the fix feature together against the current combined code, not an obsolete diff alone. Check affected regression coverage as well as the original failure; do not reopen unrelated historical findings without new evidence of a current defect.

## 3) Spawn review subagents via Task tool

For each feature needing review, spawn a subagent:

```
Task({
  subagent_type: "scrutiny-feature-reviewer",
  await: true,
  description: "Review feature <feature-id>",
  prompt: `
    You are reviewing feature "<feature-id>" for milestone "<milestone>".
    
    Feature details:
    - ID: <feature-id>
    - Description: <description>
    - Worker session: <workerSessionId>
    
    Mission dir: <missionDir>
    
    Write your review report to this path: {missionDir}/validation/<milestone>/scrutiny/reviews/<feature-id>.json
    
    [For re-runs only:]
    This is reviewing a FIX for a prior failure. Also examine:
    - Original failed feature: <original-feature-id>
    - Prior review: {missionDir}/validation/<milestone>/scrutiny/reviews/<original-feature-id>.json
    
    You must review the fix feature's transcript skeleton and BOTH features' diffs
    to determine if the fix adequately addresses the original failure.
  `
})
```

**Spawn subagents in parallel** when reviewing multiple features.

Wait for all subagents to complete before proceeding.

## 4) Synthesize and triage shared state observations

Read all review reports from `{missionDir}/validation/<milestone>/scrutiny/reviews/`.

### 4a) Determine pass/fail

- Adjudicate and deduplicate findings against current code and the approved requirements. A reviewer's severity label is a claim to evaluate, not an automatic veto.
- Blocking findings need a concrete unmet approved requirement, failure path, or material correctness/security risk. Missing required validation is also a blocker; stronger optional proof, procedural preferences, and documentation polish are not automatically blockers.
- Resolve duplicates, already-fixed findings, and unsupported claims with a short rationale in the synthesis. Keep optional guidance as recommendations, not acceptance criteria or mandatory follow-up work.
- If any confirmed blocking issue remains: `status: "fail"`. Otherwise, if required programmatic validators passed: `status: "pass"`. Preserve raw review results and explain any disagreement.

### 4b) Triage shared state observations

Collect all `sharedStateObservations` from reviewer reports. Deduplicate across reviews (multiple reviewers may flag the same thing).

For each observation, apply your judgment using these first principles about what belongs where:

- **`services.yaml`**: Operational commands and services that workers need to run. Factual, mechanical. Source of truth for how to execute things.
- **`library/`**: Factual knowledge about the codebase discovered during work — patterns, quirks, env vars, API conventions, online documentation. Reference material, not instructions.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: Normative guidance from orchestrator to workers — conventions, boundaries, rules. The orchestrator's voice.
- **Skills** (`{missionDir}/skills/`): Procedural instructions for worker types. Should reflect what actually works, not idealized procedure.

Triage each observation into one of three buckets:

**Apply now** (services.yaml and library updates you're confident about):
These are factual, low-risk, and within your domain.
For library entries, check if the knowledge is already documented.
For services.yaml entries, validate against the manifest schema before applying:
- **Services** require: `start`, `stop`, `healthcheck` (port hardcoded in all three command strings), `port` (declares which port for conflict detection), `depends_on`
- **Commands** require: the command string
- Check that no existing service/command uses the same name or port
- Only additive changes — never overwrite existing entries

**Recommend to orchestrator** (AGENTS.md and skill changes):
These are normative decisions that belong to the orchestrator. For each recommendation, include:
- What should change and why
- The evidence from reviews (which features, what pattern)
- Whether it's a systemic issue (same problem across multiple features/workers)
The orchestrator will decide whether to act.

**Reject** (ambiguous, duplicate, or wrong):
Record what you rejected and why. If a candidate is ambiguous or you're unsure, reject it — it's better to skip than to apply something wrong.

## 5) Write synthesis report

Create/update synthesis file:

```json
// {missionDir}/validation/<milestone>/scrutiny/synthesis.json
{
  "milestone": "<milestone>",
  "round": 1,  // increment on re-runs
  "status": "pass" | "fail",
  "validatorsRun": {
    "test": { "passed": true, "command": "...", "exitCode": 0 },
    "typecheck": { "passed": true, "command": "...", "exitCode": 0 },
    "lint": { "passed": true, "command": "...", "exitCode": 0 }
  },
  "reviewsSummary": {
    "total": 5,
    "passed": 4,
    "failed": 1,
    "failedFeatures": ["checkout-reserve-inventory"]
  },
  "blockingIssues": [
    { "featureId": "...", "severity": "blocking", "description": "..." }
  ],
  "appliedUpdates": [
    // services.yaml / library updates you applied directly
    { "target": "services.yaml|library", "description": "...", "sourceFeature": "..." }
  ],
  "suggestedGuidanceUpdates": [
    // AGENTS.md / skill changes recommended to the orchestrator
    {
      "target": "AGENTS.md",
      "suggestion": "Add boundary: do not modify shared test fixtures in tests/fixtures/. Workers should create feature-specific fixtures instead.",
      "evidence": "Features auth-flow and user-profile both modified tests/fixtures/users.json with conflicting shapes, breaking each other's tests.",
      "isSystemic": true
    }
  ],
  "rejectedObservations": [
    { "observation": "...", "reason": "duplicate|ambiguous|already-documented" }
  ],
  "previousRound": null  // or path to previous synthesis on re-runs
}
```

## 6) Return to orchestrator

Call `EndFeatureRun` with `returnToOrchestrator: true` (always).

- If any blocking issues: `successState: "failure"`
- If all passed: `successState: "success"`

Include the synthesis file path in `handoff.salientSummary` (e.g., "Synthesis: {missionDir}/validation/<milestone>/scrutiny/synthesis.json").

Put only confirmed actionable defects/blockers in `discoveredIssues` and unmet assigned work in `whatWasLeftUndone`. Optional recommendations remain in the synthesis (for example, `suggestedGuidanceUpdates` or a deferred disposition in `rejectedObservations`), not in actionable handoff fields. Do not call failure merely to force optional work into the queue.

The orchestrator will:
- Read `synthesis.json` for the full report
- Create fix features for blocking issues
- Review `suggestedGuidanceUpdates` and update AGENTS.md / skills as appropriate
- The user-testing-validator (next feature) will run automatically after you complete

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints

make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
```

(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)

reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
```

## 3
# Rust conventions

**What belongs here:** how Rust code is written, named, tested and committed in this repository, with the
pinned versions and the architectural invariants a worker must keep. Sources: `AGENTS.md`, `SPEC.md` §4
and §6, `architecture.md` §1, §13, §14, the git hooks under `.githooks/`.

**What does not belong here:** environment facts (`environment.md`), test procedures that drive the
running app (`user-testing.md`), integration mechanics (`integration-and-boundaries.md`).

## Edition, lints, formatting

- Rust 2024 edition, toolchain 1.99.1 from `rust-toolchain.toml` (rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not
  change the toolchain without a decision file.
- `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors: `make lint` runs
  `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity`;
  CI sets `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"`.
- `make fmt-check` (`cargo fmt --all -- --check`) is part of `make check` and of the pre-commit hook.
- `cargo machete` runs in CI from S (B-014): no unused dependency.

## Naming

- Standard Rust: `snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE` consts.
- Event kinds mirror PRD §7 names in `snake_case` turned into variants: `finding.blocking` becomes
  `EventKind::FindingBlocking`, `unknown.event` becomes `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`. Lane and role enums
  use the PRD's words.
- Crate paths are a contract probed by the Makefile and CI: `crates/observatory-core`, `crates/observatory-cli`,
  `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri` (package `observatory-app`), `apps/observatory-app/ui` (package
  `observatory-ui`). Keep them.

## Tests

- Unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs` (`replay_s.rs`, `mapping.rs`, `store.rs`, `attach_latency.rs`, `view.rs`,
  `rpc.rs`, `control.rs`, `forge.rs`, `oracle.rs`, `telemetry.rs`; CLI: `crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs`
  with `assert_cmd`). Fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`.
- Test functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`,
  `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()`, `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file()`.
- UI logic is unit-tested in `core::view`; there is no wasm test runner. The UI crate gets `cargo check`
  only.
- Coverage scope is `observatory-core` only: `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80`,
  reported in S, enforced from M0. It runs alone (see `services.yaml`).
- Golden files (`<fixture>.events.json`) are regenerated only with
  `OBSERVATORY_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping` and a reviewer read.
- Flaky timing tests (attach latency) are reported with their `p50/p95/max`, never retried silently.

## Red before green (rule 1)

The failing test is committed before the code that makes it pass; the scrutiny validator checks that the
red run exists in the worker log. Pattern per feature:

1. Write the test, run it, paste the failing output into the handoff.
2. Commit the red test. Subject example: `test(core): red — rework_window_closes_on_resolution`.
3. Write the code, run the test green, run `make check`.
4. Commit the code. Subject example: `feat(core): close rework windows on resolution — green`.

Commit rules enforced by `.githooks/commit-msg`: subject non-empty and at most 72 characters, no
`WIP`/`fixup!`/`squash!`. Every agent commit carries the trailer
`Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`. Pass

- I1: `observatory-core` is synchronous. No `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API; tokio lives only in

- I2: the UI holds no logic. Card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details and library entries are
